scope_note: These cases test principal separation and acceptance on top of the revision-pinned v1 cryptographic verifier. They do not change CAID action material and do not turn OAuth sub or SPT human_anchor into human authorization.

vectors.input: A verified OAuth Txn-Token carries the closed v2 relationship claim. Logical agent, live workload instance, OAuth client, delegating principal, executor, and tool all match relying-party pins; the WIT confirmation key thumbprint and SPT tool independently agree.
The native bundle verifies, but the signed relationship claim or one required relationship member is absent or malformed.
The logical agent is unchanged but the signed live workload instance differs from the pinned instance and WIT subject relationship.
OAuth sub is unchanged while the signed OAuth client identity differs from the client pinned for this grant.
The same sub is replayed under a different grant type or a different declared meaning of sub.
The live workload instance claim names a confirmation-key thumbprint that does not match both the relying-party pin and the verified WIT cnf.jwk.
Authorization-server metadata and verification material are discovered, but the server and its claim semantics are absent from the relying party's constructor pins.
The signed relationship claim names a different tool from the independently verified SPT intent used by the material action.
The signed executor identity differs from the executor pinned together with the OAuth and WIMSE audiences.
